title: pod — Sat, Oct 24
notes_html:
Projects

You have a few things waiting today. Most urgent is the calculators project.

For calculators, the photo test is due this week. You need to create a dedicated AI key with a provider-side spending cap of fifteen dollars or less, then run the test with two or three friends. The pre-order launch setup also needs you in the PreProduct and Notifications admin screens before the first real listing. You're also asked whether to reword the decision record so three items don't read as confirmed. And the federal communications check can't start before October thirtieth, since the vote is October twenty-ninth.

For AlphaThread, three blocked queue tasks need your answers, with recommended answers already filled in. They cover the scale route for the parity results, repair of partial daily candles, and handle discovery. Also, the fifth and last live paper session is Monday. After that, the final validation run is yours to start, and it closes out the run.

Now the projects. Starting with AlphaThread, which moved from blocked to attention. Session four of five is done. The underlying stopped at the open and there was one open. The books agreed all day, with twenty-five checkpoints, no breaks and no faults. Your runner has been up about eighty-six hours, the database was written to this morning, and there have been no alerts. On the operator interface branch, the live success criterion now passes, and the authentication page offers re-authentication before the refresh token expires. One oddity: no task completion events were recorded for the work queue. Next is Monday's session, then final validation.

Calculators had a good overnight run, with seven tasks done. There was research on the trademark position for the ChatGPT calculator keyword page, and the low-credit rule is built. The emailed export link is built too. The drafts now treat pre-order and waitlist together, and the theme has a waitlist form next to pre-order. There was also research on short-form editing and scheduling tools for the Instagram and TikTok pipeline, plus the over the air update check and a firmware spec catch-up. The five new database migrations exist only locally. Queued next are research on a free-first short-form stack, a draft keyword page for the AI calculator with chat, and a publishing runbook with a signing-key rotation plan. With your okay, the migrations can go to the dev project and the changed functions can roll out. Two things are stuck. The export confirmation page needs a Supabase custom domain, and the price is still to be checked. The privacy recheck still needs a publish date. The AI provider retention questions from yesterday no longer appear on your list.

IG ideas ran fine at six. It found no new posts, so no ideas today. The inbox holds forty-eight ideas, with one queued.

Discordscrape has fifteen commits on master. Live signals now come with phone alerts and a hook, along with new commands to watch, peek, follow, and capture live chat. There's also a way to search and read the collected corpus. Free channels from Invest With Mordy and The Flow Project were added.

Pod now records run start, run end and publish events to the shared operations log. Reel-inbox does the same for ingested, filed and finished items, and it now marks notes as requested when you send a queue-this message.

The remaining AlphaThread worktrees are idle and clean, covering pricing ladder, charts, health, recorder, runner, interface, docs, and the worker.

Overall, the live run is steady, and what's holding things up is mostly your answers and admin steps.

title: pod — Mon, Oct 19
notes_html:
Projects

Here is what needs you today, starting with AlphaThread.

First, check that your runner is really active. The process has been up for about forty-three hours, but the newest log's last line says the runner finished, written about sixteen hours ago. It is unclear whether that is normal.

Second, the five-session paper run needs you to start counting today. Five consecutive trading sessions begin this Monday, with at least one open and close. Then you repeat the success criterion check with a position open, and then run the final validation. One catch: the Schwab token was assumed to lapse on October eighteenth, and it is unknown whether it was renewed.

For kalq, there are four asks. First, the privacy follow-ups. You need to say which ad pixel events and hashed email go to ad partners. Confirm pixels by default in the US, but only after accept in the EU and UK. You also need to settle the thirteen-plus and under-sixteen position, the split between eighteen-plus in the Terms of Sale and thirteen-plus for accounts, and that export happens only through the account page. These unblock the privacy policy publish and the alert work.

Second, answer the firmware spec questions: whether over the air updates are a launch requirement, the update signing key, the API domain, and the photo limit. They block the firmware task. Also say what came out of the Shenzhen meeting on October eighteenth, because the outcome is not recorded.

Third, give the alert email address and sender, and OK a push to the dev theme plus turning on the customer privacy setting so the footer link tests can run.

Fourth, nothing to do today, but the FCC vote is October twenty-ninth, and the re-check cannot start before October thirtieth.

Now AlphaThread. Three commits landed on October eighteenth. The OptionsDX importer is merged, and that roadmap item is marked done. There are no task changes. Seventy-one tasks are done and two are open, the paper run and the final validation, and only you can close both. After the run, the validation script gets run requiring completeness, and the counts get recorded. The next spec after merge will be number twenty, the pricing ladder. Health is at warning, and it comes down to the runner question. There were no alerts in the last day and no collection errors.

On kalq, the status is blocked. The overnight run finished six tasks and made ten commits. The privacy policy now reflects four newly recorded decisions. The backend has the thirteen-plus tick, consent purge, and an alert stub. Retention purges are in: AI requests after thirteen months, webhook payloads after forty-five or ninety days. There is a parallel-session test for credit reserve against account deletion, footer privacy links in local theme files that are not pushed, and a stuck-reservation closer that claims before it calls, for spend safety. Tests pass: one hundred twenty-nine for functions, one hundred fifty-two for the database. Also recorded: a supplier log update and 4G and SIM feasibility research.

Next for kalq: a run-through on the Supabase dev project, a spend-reserve day test with concurrency, the real alert sender once chosen, and the dev theme link test once approved. Blocked: firmware on your answers, the FCC re-check on the date, and the privacy policy publish on a date and the open items. Not yet verified anywhere: real Supabase behavior, cron schedules, and the theme links in a browser.

In short: check the runner, start the count, and clear the kalq questions.
